title: ELP Test - Explain Image - example 7
text: ELP Test - Explain Image - example 7 This image shows a commercial airliner that has made an emergency water landing. The aircraft is floating on the water with both wings visible and largely intact. On the wings, there are groups of people standing; these are the passengers and possibly crew members who have evacuated the aircraft and are waiting for rescue.One of the over-wing emergency exit doors appears to be open, and it is likely that the other exits have been used as well. This type of emergency water landing is also known as ditching. The fact that the aircraft is still afloat suggests that the fuselage is still largely intact and that the ditching was relatively controlled, allowing for the survival of the structure upon impact with the water.There are no visible signs of fire or smoke, and the people on the wings seem to be relatively calm, which suggests that the situation, while serious, is currently stable. The body of water appears to be relatively calm as well, which would have been beneficial during the landing and evacuation process.From a small details perspective, the image is taken from a distance, in daylight, and the visibility is clear, aiding in the rescue efforts that would follow such an event. The location of the aircraft in the water relative to any land is not visible in the image, so it's not possible to determine the proximity to potential rescue services.
